title: Rajma
subtitle: North Indian kidney bean curry
excerpt: The beloved kidney bean curry of Punjab: kidney beans simmered in a deep, spiced tomato and onion gravy until the sauce clings to every bean. A dal-style dish with substantial body, eaten with rice for the iconic rajma-chawal combination.

recipe.sourceNotes: Rajma is the most important bean dish of north Indian cooking, particularly associated with the Punjab and with Punjabi communities across India and worldwide. The word simply means kidney beans. Rajma-chawal (kidney beans with rice) is to north India what dal-chawal is to the rest of the subcontinent: the essential comfort combination, the dish cooked every week in millions of households, the taste of home. The dish uses kidney beans, either from dried (soaked overnight and cooked from scratch) or tinned. The gravy is built on the north Indian masala base of fried onion, tomato, ginger, and garlic, spiced with cumin, coriander, garam masala, and amchur (dried mango powder) for tartness. The beans should be cooked until very soft and the gravy should be thick enough to coat the beans; watery rajma is under-cooked rajma.

content.text: Cook the onion until it is very deeply golden; this is the foundation of the curry's depth. A pale-fried onion produces a flat, raw-tasting curry. The tomatoes should cook until completely broken down and the oil separates from the masala before the beans go in. If using dried kidney beans, never cook them without first boiling hard for 10 minutes to destroy the natural toxins.

items.preparation: 2 tins, drained and rinsed; or 350 g dried, soaked overnight and boiled until soft

content.text: Heat the oil in a heavy pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds. Add the onion and cook for 18 to 20 minutes, stirring regularly, until very deeply golden brown. Do not rush; the depth of colour determines the depth of the curry. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.

Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric, and chilli powder and cook for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes, reduce the heat, and cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes break down completely and the oil separates to the surface of the masala.

Add the kidney beans, 200 ml water, and salt. Stir well. Mash about a quarter of the beans against the side of the pan with the back of a spoon to thicken the sauce. Simmer for 15 minutes until the sauce is thick and coats the beans. Stir in the garam masala. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve over basmati rice scattered with fresh coriander.
